frames.title: Lesson 127 · Lexical precision: convince × persuade — meanings

body: **Texto do dia:** conto e trecho de peça.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo distinguir convince (mudar uma crença) de persuade (levar a agir) em uma cena de teatro, escolhendo o verbo e a estrutura corretos.

body: Esta aula treina **ler textos curtos e achar informação (IELTS Reading, TOEFL Reading)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

frames.title: Reading · A scene from a play

blocks.title: Scene: The Last Juror
paras: (A jury room. Eight jurors are seated; ELENA stands by the window.)
ELENA: I am **convinced** he is innocent, but I know that **convincing** you of it will take all night.
MARCO: You **can’t persuade** me to change my vote on a feeling.

ELENA: I don’t want to **persuade** you **to** do anything. I want to **convince** you **that** the timeline is impossible. **Look**: the shop closed at nine, and the witness says she saw him at nine-fifteen.
MARCO: (after a pause) …You’ve **convinced** me **of** one thing: we should read the testimony again.
ELENA: **That is all I ask.** And if the facts **persuade** you **to** vote differently, **so be it**.

items.q: Elena has no opinion about the case.
items.why: I am convinced he is innocent.

items.q: Marco agrees to read the testimony again.
items.why: we should read the testimony again.

items.q: Elena wants to change Marco’s vote by emotion.
items.why: She wants to convince him with the timeline.

blocks.body: **Convince** = produzir **crença**; **persuade** = produzir **ação**. Com *that* os dois funcionam; com *to + verbo* use **persuade**. *Convince to do* é considerado menos formal.
✗ *I convinced him to go.* é comum, mas em prova prefira ✓ *I persuaded him to go.*

items.s: She wants to ___ him that the timeline is impossible. (convince)
You can’t ___ me to change my vote. (persuade)
If the facts persuade you ___ vote differently, so be it. (to)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.ans: Fine I'm open to being convinced
items.pt: Certo. Estou aberto a ser convencido.

body: **Be dead set against** — ser totalmente contra
**Fine. I’m open to being convinced.** — Certo. Estou aberto a ser convencido.
**I want to convince you that the timeline is impossible.** — Quero convencê-lo de que a cronologia é impossível.
**You can’t persuade me to change my vote on a feeling.** — Você não me persuade a mudar o voto com base num sentimento.

forms: He cajoled the board into agreeing.
Ele persuadiu o conselho com lisonjas.

blocks.title: Jury room
lines: I want to convince you that the timeline is impossible.
Quero convencê-lo de que a cronologia é impossível.
You can’t persuade me to change my vote on a feeling.
Você não me persuade a mudar o voto com base num sentimento.
Then let the facts persuade you to read it again.
Então deixe que os fatos o persuadam a ler de novo.
Fine. I’m open to being convinced.
Certo. Estou aberto a ser convencido.

items.label: Ajuste refinado de entonação
items.note: Ajuste refinado de entonação: pequenas variações de altura e de ritmo mudam a atitude (cortesia, ironia, reserva, compromisso) sem mudar as palavras.
words: I suppose that’s one way to put it. ↘↗ (reserva)
Well, that’s ONE way to put it. ↘ (ironia)

prompts.model: She convinced me that the plan was sound.
He persuaded the board to wait.
I am convinced that we are right.

blocks.task: Write 5 sentences using convince and persuade correctly about a jury or committee decision.
blocks.model: The lawyer convinced the jury that the timeline was wrong. She then persuaded them to review the testimony. I am convinced that careful reading changes minds. No speech could persuade me to vote without evidence. It takes facts to convince, and patience to persuade.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
